report: Local LLM (Ollama / Llama) behind a Python API: security BEFORE vs AFTER

legend.PASSED: the system withstood the attack, or served a legitimate request correctly
legend.FAILED: the attack worked, or a legitimate request was refused

meta.demo_accounts: alice, bob, carol (passwords in demo/credentials.json; stored hashed in data/users.json)
meta.note: Every scenario is sent identically to both apps; only the server differs.

summary.before: 19 of 28 scenarios FAILED on the vulnerable app
summary.after: 1 of 28 scenarios FAILED on the hardened app

cases.name: Prompt injection
cases.what_it_is: Text typed by the user overrides the developer's instructions, so the bot does what the attacker says or goes outside its job.

why_vulnerable: vulnerable_app.py pastes SYSTEM_PROMPT and the user's text into ONE prompt string, so the model cannot tell instructions from data.
Nothing checks what the user's message is trying to do.
The model is not deterministic, so each prompt is tried up to 4 times and the report says how often it worked.

guardrails_applied.what_we_did: Before the chat model sees a message, a separate Llama call reads the chatbot's own rules together with the message and answers, in a fixed JSON format, four yes/no questions about its MEANING (does it override the rules or give a new role? dictate or control the reply? ask for instructions or secrets? is it unrelated to Acme?) and then ALLOWED or BLOCKED. BLOCKED requests get HTTP 400 and never reach the chat model. There is no keyword or regex list anywhere: paraphrases, other languages and obfuscated spellings are judged on what they mean.

guardrails_applied.control: The guard cannot be talked into leaking
guardrails_applied.what_we_did: The guard sees only the public rules, never the confidential note; the user text is delimited and treated as data; output is forced into a JSON schema with an ALLOWED/BLOCKED enum at temperature 0; if the guard cannot answer, the request is refused (fails closed).
Unicode NFKC folding and removal of control / zero-width characters, so the guard sees obfuscated text as a human reads it. No words are matched.
System instructions and user text go as separate `system` / `user` messages to /api/chat; model and parameters are fixed by the server; unknown request fields are rejected.

cases.known_limits: The guard is a language model, so it can be wrong in both directions: see semantic_guard_evaluation for measured numbers on prompts it was not tuned on. It adds one extra model call to every request.

cases.name: Unauthenticated endpoint access
cases.what_it_is: Anyone who can reach the port can use the chatbot and internal endpoints.

why_vulnerable: No authentication on any endpoint, including /debug/config.
Credentials, if sent, are simply ignored, so a wrong password is as good as a right one.

cases.known_limits: HTTP Basic over plain HTTP is only acceptable on localhost; use TLS in production.

cases.name: Rate limiting / resource exhaustion
cases.what_it_is: A caller can make the server, and the model behind it, do unbounded work and starve other users.

why_vulnerable: Request bodies of any size are read and sent to the model.
The caller controls max_tokens, including unlimited generation.
No rate limit, no cap on simultaneous model calls, no timeout.

guardrails_applied.what_we_did: Bodies above 4096 bytes get 413, including chunked uploads that send no Content-Length header.
message <= 1000 characters, max_tokens <= 200; larger values are rejected (422).
Sliding window of 30 requests per minute per authenticated user, then 429 with Retry-After.
At most 2 requests use the model at once; extra requests get an immediate 503 instead of queueing without bound.
60 s upstream timeout, num_ctx fixed at 2048, no streaming.

cases.name: Context / system prompt leakage
cases.what_it_is: The system prompt or other hidden context (here a marker and an escalation passcode) is exposed through endpoints, errors or the model's own answers.

why_vulnerable: The API docs / schema are public.
Upstream errors are returned verbatim with the full prompt, and the caller can choose the model.
Nothing checks what the model says before it is returned.

guardrails_applied.what_we_did: /debug/*, /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json are removed.
Validation, upstream and unexpected errors return a short code (E_INVALID, E_UPSTREAM, E_INTERNAL); details go to the server log only; invalid input is never echoed.
A request that includes `model` (or any unknown field) is rejected.
Requests that try to extract the instructions, notes or codes are judged by meaning and blocked before reaching the chat model (same guard as case 1).

Every model reply is compared with this deployment's own protected strings (the confidential note, the passcode and each sentence of the system prompt) after normalising; a match is replaced by a fixed refusal. This checks for the deployment's own secret, it is not a keyword classifier of user prompts.
